- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 316be321ef2405a12e8d016f07b25fad7039b4f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.

```sh

git fetch origin 6e733d5c38ffa93e254321ab268288f1116be875 && git checkout 6e733d5c38ffa93e254321ab268288f1116be875

git fetch origin 316be321ef2405a12e8d016f07b25fad7039b4f9 5f628a7600b09ad3b20062ff1e2d0fbf6dec6dfb && git checkout -B drift-repro 316be321ef2405a12e8d016f07b25fad7039b4f9 && git merge --no-ff 5f628a7600b09ad3b20062ff1e2d0fbf6dec6dfb
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f628a7600b09ad3b20062ff1e2d0fbf6dec6dfb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21724 (body; triage `5979725587`; claim `5979764563`; dev report `5980359706`; ACCEPT `5980375306`), PR #21740 (body, 11-file list, net diff against the merge-base `316be321ef`: +435 / -37, byte-equal to the files API), the 40 check-runs on the head (every one `completed`; the latest run per name is `success`, or `skipped` for the opt-in / path-filtered ones; all seven required contexts green), and the cross-lane declaration `5979774266` on #6017. Head content was read with `git show` on objects already present locally; nothing was fetched, checked out, built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Both doors serve the engine code, no status moved — right.** `classifyResumeResult` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`) is the one classifier for `POST /automation/:name/runs/:runId/resume` and for the MCP `resume_run` tool (`mcp.ts:964`, through `resumeDoorError` into the same `deps.error`). Each of the six coded rows now returns `details: { code }`; `buildApiError` (`error-envelope.ts`) promotes `details.code` into `error.code` verbatim and drops the then-empty `details`. The six row statuses in `RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS` are unchanged in the diff (only the declaration gained `export`), the classifier's branch predicate is unchanged, the FLOW_FAILED exit already carried `details.code`, and `service-automation` is untouched. Wire moves, each checked against `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` to `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` / `INVALID_SIGNAL`; 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` to `RUN_NOT_FOUND`; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` to `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`; 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` to `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS`; 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` unchanged. Accept set: nothing accepted is now refused and nothing refused is now accepted.
2. **Every wire code is ledgered under its owner, and the one row is the only spec-side change — right.** `INVALID_SIGNAL`, `RUN_NOT_FOUND`, `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS`, `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` were already under `@objectstack/service-automation`; `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` joins them there (the stamp site is that package's `engine.ts`, so the owner key is right; provenance gate green); `PERMISSION_DENIED` is a standard member. The only `packages/spec` path in the diff is `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (+1 / -0), exactly what `5979774266` declared. Public surface: `ErrorCode`, and so `ApiErrorSchema.code`, gains one member and loses none. The two `content/docs/references/api/*.mdx` edits are the generator's output for that row (one bullet each, `+320 more` to `+321 more`), under an AUTO-GEN tree, not hand-edited.
3. **The `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` row deletion is forced, not a widening — right.** The gate's own header says a registration makes the stamp site disappear from the scan, and `reconcile` then fails a declared row whose site is gone as `stale-row` with the text "delete the row". Keeping the row would also have left a `why` that reads "this string is not what lands in `error.code`", which this diff makes false. `UNREGISTERED_CODE_SITES` shrinks by one and gains nothing; the sibling row's `why` edit is prose only.
4. **`ResumeRefusal.details` required changes no exported type a consumer compiles against — right, and inside the declared semver.** `ResumeRefusal` and `RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS` live in `domains/automation.ts`; the runtime package's only entry is `src/index.ts` via `./dist/index.js`, which re-exports nothing from `domains/` (the only non-test importers of the module are `endpoint-executor.ts` and `http-dispatcher.ts`, taking other names), and runtime carries no api-surface snapshot. The narrowing is module-internal; its two consumers compile (`mcp.ts`'s `resumeDoorError` takes the wider `details?: Record`), and `TypeScript Type Check` is green on the head. Not breaking; `minor` covers it.
5. **The 503 and 409 moves fall inside triage's stated direction — right, no separate ruling needed.** Triage `5979725587` directs "each refusal row carries its engine code in `details.code`, so the builder never derives it from the status", with no row carved out. The 17.1.0 CHANGELOG in both `runtime` and `client` names `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` (409) and `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) among the refusals that "keep their own code"; the client `resume()` JSDoc names the same four retryables; the engine's own `RETRYABLE_RESUME_REFUSAL_CODES` is exactly that set; both codes were already ledgered. The changeset table and the PR body name both moves. The seat's ACCEPT dispositioned them the same way.
6. **Pins match the card's "Done when" and triage's three pins — right.** Per row: key parses as `ErrorCode` (a new row without a registration reds by name), the REST door serves the code and the body parses under `ApiErrorSchema`, and a separate case holds status, message and empty `details`; a floor pins the six rows. `http-dispatcher.test.ts` replaces every `.not.toBe('FLOW_FAILED')` with the code. `mcp-resume-run.test.ts` names the code per row door-against-door and re-pins the CONTROL case that had pinned the defect. The client pin drives the real engine, dispatcher and client over built `dist` for all four of the card's refusals, asserting `err.code`, the wire code, the `ApiErrorSchema` parse, the status, the run still `paused`, and a corrected resume completing where the flow survives. `client.test.ts`'s mocked body moves from `NOT_FOUND` (a code no door answers) to `RUN_NOT_FOUND`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21724-resume-refusal-codes.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/runtime: minor`; body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, the per-row before/after table, and the "nothing accepted is refused; the run stays paused" statement. Package by package against the diff: `spec` publishes one new `ErrorCode` member and removes none (widening, `minor` is the floor the rule sets for `yes`); `runtime` publishes a resume door whose answer set gains five registered codes with no status or accept-set move and one internal type tightened (widening, `minor`); `client` ships test-only changes (`src/index.ts` untouched), so no entry is due; `service-automation` is untouched. No `(narrowing)` arm, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — matches the PR body, the claim and the cross-lane declaration.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. Dev deviations, each answered: (1) the two generated reference pages are `gen:docs` output for the one row — accepted; (2) the vocabulary row deletion is gate-forced (①.3) — accepted; (3) the MCP CONTROL re-pin replaces a pin on the defect; `mcp.ts` untouched — accepted; (4) the two extra rows are inside triage's direction (①.5) — accepted; (5) the full local suite ran one test-only commit before the head and CI `Test Core` is green on the head itself, which supersedes the local reading — accepted; (6) attribution form and (7) the full local lint are outside this contract and consistent with the stated form — noted; (8) the dispatch's comment count (3 vs 2) is bookkeeping — noted. Dispatch fences held: no `service-automation` edit, no status move, no suspension change, no `packages/spec` path beyond the declared row. Out-of-scope finding: the MCP `resume_run` door's own pre-engine refusals (its single not-resumable 404, the non-screen 409, the admission 403) still carry status-derived codes, so an unknown run reads `RUN_NOT_FOUND` over REST and `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` over MCP; `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` promises parity only for the engine's answers, and `mcp-resume-run.test.ts` (c) pins that 404 as the door's deliberate non-disclosure envelope — an observation recorded in the PR's acceptance notes, not a contract violation; not escalated.
